713428.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pʰérō, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰéreti. Cognates include Old English beran (English bear), Latin ferō, Sanskrit भरति (bhárati), Old Armenian բերեմ (berem), and Albanian bie.

713494.t: From φιλόσοφος (phĭlósophos, “lover of knowledge or wisdom”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā), from φίλος (phĭ́los, “beloved; loving”) + σοφός (sophós, “skilled with handcrafts; wise”).

713433.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pʰéugō, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰewg- (“to flee”). Related to φυγή (phugḗ, verbal noun) and Latin fugiō.

713442.t: Apparently from a stem φθεγ- (phtheg-) with added ablaut and nasalization, of unclear further origin.

713495.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *bʰil- Proto-Indo-European *-os Proto-Indo-European *bʰil-o-s Ancient Greek φίλος (phĭ́los) Ancient Greek σοφός (sophós) Ancient Greek φιλόσοφος From φίλος (phĭ́los, “loving”) + σοφός (sophós, “wise”).

713436.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pʰā́mā, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₂-meh₂, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₂- (“to speak”). By surface analysis, a full-grade deverbal of φημί (phēmĭ́, “to say; to explain; to argue”).

713450.t: According to Beekes, from a Proto-Indo-European *dʰgʷʰen-, albeit with no certain adduced cognates.

713453.t: According to Beekes, probably from Pre-Greek or some other language, based on the interchange of suffixes in the Mycenaean cognates.

713447.t: Nominal form of the verb φθέγγομαι (phthéngomai, “to utter a sound, raise one's voice”).

713445.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʷʰtʰéřřō, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰgʷʰér-ye-ti, from *dʰgʷʰer- (“flow, diverge; perish”) via the middle form φθείρομαι (phtheíromai, “to be destroyed, perish”) with new active meaning “destroy”.

713439.t: Apparently from a Proto-Indo-European *dʰgʷʰh₂- (“to come near, nearly reach, pass”), and cognate with a Sanskrit धग्नु (dhagnu). However, such a Sanskrit term does not seem to be attested in Sanskrit dictionaries.

713443.t: From the root of φθέγγομαι (phthéngomai, “to make a sound”) + -μα (-ma).

713404.t: Of unknown origin. Traditionally compared with Lithuanian spingė́ti, spingiù (“to glitter”), as well as with Old High German funko (“spark”), but this suggestion is impossible in view of the initial stops.

713441.t: From φθείρω (phtheírō, “to spoil, ruin”) + -τός (-tós, adjectival suffix).

713426.t: From φέρω (phérō, “bring”) + -νή (-nḗ, “a suffix added to verbal stems or adjectives to form feminine nouns.”) The nasal-suffix is also present in Old Armenian բեռն (beṙn) and Lithuanian bernas.

713446.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dʰgʷʰey- (“to decline, disappear”). Cognate with Sanskrit क्षिणाति (kṣiṇā́ti, “to destroy, ruin”).

713408.t: φειδός (pheidós) + the same suffix found in ἁμαρτωλός (hamartōlós, “sinful”).

713406.t: From Proto-Indo-European *bʰéydt (“to split”). Cognate with Sanskrit भेदति (bhedati, “to split”) and Gothic 𐌱𐌴𐌹𐍄𐌰𐌽 (beitan, “to bite”).

713482.t: From φιλο- (philo-) + the root of μανθάνω (manthánō) + -ής (-ḗs).
